title: Teaching himself from piano books and practicing with Harry
summary: Love tells how he studied Cecilia's piano books in a wash shed as a boy and later practiced the Red Book every day with clarinetist Harry in Alexandria.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I catch one band maybe play one or two of them, and the other band maybe play two or three of them. I used to study them books. Cecilia kind of had books like that, but just for piano, you know. And boy she could play some piano. She learned that in England. And she finished college over there. She come over here and went to Boston Conservatory. Studied all over again and learned them books. And threw them in the wash shed, you know. In the wash house. They had a regular wash house. They had a bell from his house to mine and called me when they were going out. Maybe I'd have to go around and hitch the buggy up or something. When they'd be gone, I'd eat that wash shed. I'd get me a mattress down, put it on the floor and get one of them big books there. Me and that book all day looking at it, you know. I was trying to make out that music, but I couldn't read so well. And I'd spell like the devil. Man, I was making notes there and coming after whistling and singing. Then when I learned how to play cornet I used to try to play them, but you see it was piano music and I had to raise the guitar and it'd run too high. I couldn't make the notes. I'd come down and make it, you know. I got all confused. And when I got to Alexander they had those red books you see, but they couldn't get no cornet player to play them. I dived in there and me and Harry used to practice every day and say, eat your breakfast and come right on around to my house. And just like a man working, me and him would blow their antics, 12 o'clock and get dinner and come back, finish the evening. And man, we got something on it. Harry bought him on it. He climbed it and he had a B2 Albert system. So he changed that system. He was a great clarinet player. He got a baron system, A and B, and sold his old clarinet. Then we practiced showing up then because he had to learn that baron system, you see. Albert is different. And he used to play over in the District Cross to buy every night. You know, when you play every night that way you can track a lot of stuff. Playing them red books, you know.
